headline: Result Update

highlights: Important Data • Consolidated revenue grew by 36% to ₹1,088crs.

On a like-to-like basis, considering the previous period revenue of Axiom and IncNut Digital, consolidated sales grew by 24%, and domestic business grew 32% with a volume growth of 26%. • The sharp Q2 gross-margin contraction was primarily driven by an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-margin strategic investments.
Management believes the margin pressure is transitional rather than structural and expects these investments to achieve high single-digit EBITDA margins over the medium to long term.

Despite these pressures, EBITDA grew by 25% to ₹222crs, and profit before tax grew by 29% to ₹194crs. • Profit after tax stood at ₹ 144crs, lower by 3%, and that is largely due to the normalization of the effective tax rate following the phasing out of fiscal benefits.
valuation: While this new line targets the mass market, the company simultaneously introduced its premium Kesh King Scalp First range exclusively through modern trade and e-commerce channels. • Organised channels are now 37% of the domestic business.
Persistent execution challenges continue to weigh on Emami’s valuation.
watch: Outlook and other points • Second-half growth guidance is 18–20% for the total business. • Rural demand is mixed.
At 20x estimated FY28 earnings, the stock trades at a significant discount to most FMCG peers, partly reflecting the high seasonality risk in its portfolio and near-term margin pressure.
